subject: Recap: latency & throughput — hosting path options and pilot
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastlanecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps on latency/throughput choices

Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we have the same frame: 

- What we heard: Fastlane is planning to use Redwood for checkout scoring and recommendation enrichments. Critical windows are flash sales (peak traffic) and normal checkout flow.
- Current target: you mentioned a P95 end-to-end latency target of ~120ms on checkout interactions; you said 80–100ms would be ideal for inference-only.
- QPS shape: steady-state around 200–300 qps, but spikes up to ~800 qps during promotions and you flagged an internal worst-case of ~1,200 qps for short bursts.
- Data residency: US only.

Want to clarify two things so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private:
1) Is the 120ms target end-to-end (client → app → inference → client) or solely the inference component? If end-to-end, what proportion (ms) is your application backend currently contributing?
2) For the burst behavior (800–1,200 qps), how long do those peaks typically last (minutes vs hours)?

Attached a small template (pilot-qps-sample.csv) — if you can fill the 24-hour per-minute QPS profile it helps our infra team size a pilot.

Immediate recommendation options for next step (pick one):
A) Short engineering Q&A (30m) with Neha (infra) to validate latencies and sizing — low lift, we give a path recommendation.
B) 2-week pilot on Hosted API with a dedicated concurrency reservation during promo windows (fastest time to data).
C) Capacity planning for Dedicated reserved pool if you need sustained <80ms inference P95 at 1k+ qps.

If you want, we can provision a cheap proof-of-concept on Hosted while we size Dedicated in parallel — that keeps the customer-facing flow live while we validate.

Next steps: choose A/B/C or confirm times for a 30m Q&A (Neha and Marissa will join from our side).

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai

Attachments: pilot-qps-sample.csv (CSV stub: one-line header, per-minute qps)

From: Samir Patel <samir@fastlanecommerce.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on latency/throughput choices

Thanks Avery — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications: 

- The 120ms we called out is end-to-end from the browser to the checkout microservice response. Our app stack typically adds ~30–40ms under normal load, so inference-only target to hit 120ms end-to-end would be ~80–90ms P95.
- Bursts: the promo spikes are short but intense — usually 8–20 minutes during a campaign start, though we have occasional longer promotions up to ~45 minutes. Peak QPS during those spikes can reach 1,100–1,300 qps for 10–20 minutes.
- Data residency: US-only, yes.

I've attached a 24h export from our traffic simulator (traffic-export-20250617.csv). Happy to do option A (30m Q&A) this week. Can we do Thursday 10am PT? Also curious about a very rough ballpark on price delta between Hosted with reservation vs Dedicated (monthly).

— Samir
Samir Patel, Head of Platform Engineering
Fastlane Commerce
samir@fastlanecommerce.com

Attachments: traffic-export-20250617.csv (CSV stub: lines of minute-level qps)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastlanecommerce.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on latency/throughput choices

Samir — appreciate the extra detail. High-level recommendation from infra/product:

- If your inference-only P95 requirement is ~80–90ms and bursts to 1.1–1.3k qps are short (10–20m), we generally recommend starting with Hosted API + reserved concurrency (burst reservation) and aggressive prefix/KV caching. This path gets you fastest time-to-value and lets us measure real traffic.
- If you require sustained 1k+ qps at ~80ms P95 (continuous for longer windows) or you want guaranteed latencies (SLA-backed), Dedicated reserved capacity is the right fit — it gives predictable throughput and capacity isolation.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) would only be required if you have regulatory or connectivity constraints (doesn’t sound necessary from what you shared).

I've attached a short deploy matrix that contrasts cost/latency tradeoffs (redwood-deploy-matrix.pdf). Proposed next steps:
1) 30m Q&A Thursday 10am PT (Avery + Neha + me) — confirm?
2) We'll run the traffic CSV through our sizing tool; if you pick Hosted pilot, we can stand up a pilot environment within 48 hours of getting the CSV.
3) If pilot metrics show high tail at peak, we’ll spin a Dedicated trial and capture delta.

Regarding ballpark pricing: Hosted with reservation is typically 40–60% cheaper short-term than Dedicated for bursty workloads because you pay less for idle capacity; Dedicated becomes economical when you hit sustained high throughput. We’ll give a tailored delta after we process your trace.

Let us know if Thursday works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-deploy-matrix.pdf (PDF stub: 2 pages, cost/latency table)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastlanecommerce.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on latency/throughput choices

Samir — quick technical note ahead of Thursday:

- Inference sizing assumptions: model median tokens per request ~32, typical sequence length small; those assumptions materially affect batching behavior. If you expect longer sequences for recommendations, tell us now.
- Rough latency guidance (inference-only, P95):
  * Hosted (optimized kernels, continuous batching, prefix cache): 70–140ms depending on load and sequence length. Good fit if you can tolerate P95 up to ~120ms and want quick ramp.
  * Dedicated (reserved GPU pool; tuned kernels + no noisy neighbors): 30–80ms P95 at 1k qps for typical short requests (32 tokens). This is where you see consistent sub-100ms inference.

- For short spikes (10–20m) of 1.2k qps, Hosted + reserved concurrency works well if the rest of the pipeline is tuned and you accept the P95 range above. If every ms matters during promos (and you want a strict SLA), plan on Dedicated.

Thursday 10am PT works for me — I’ll bring sizing notes and example baseline configs. Please send the CSV to sizing@redwood.ai (or I’ll pull from the thread attachment).

— Neha
Neha Kapoor | Staff Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Thanks all — Thursday at 10am PT is good. I uploaded the CSV to the Drive link you sent and copied the 24h profile into the template.

One more ask before the call: can you prepare a 1-page cost delta (Hosted reserved vs Dedicated monthly) with an example based on 1k average qps and 1.2k peak bursts? That will help my CFO greenlight a pilot.

See you Thursday — Samir
